title: Unit – 2 : Session – 9 : SLO – 2  |  Doubly Linked List — Introduction
sections: In a doubly linked list, each node contains TWO pointers.
The two pointers in a doubly linked list point to the PREVIOUS and the NEXT nodes.
The pointer to the next node in a doubly linked list is commonly called NEXT (RLINK).
The pointer to the previous node in a doubly linked list is commonly called PREV (LLINK).
In a doubly linked list, the previous pointer of the head node is always set to NULL.
In a doubly linked list, the next pointer of the tail node is always set to NULL.
Insertion at the beginning of a doubly linked list requires updating the PREV pointer of the old head node.
Deletion of a node in a doubly linked list requires adjusting the pointers of its PREVIOUS and NEXT nodes.
Traversing a doubly linked list can be done in both FORWARD and BACKWARD directions.
A doubly linked list allows for more efficient deletion operations compared to a SINGLY linked list.
